findings.rationale: A 23,176,722-byte file in the user's Downloads directory matches the byte count of the patients_full bulk export (23176722) logged at 10:26:38, and it was the size of the flow that left the host at 10:27:48. Its presence in Downloads before the outbound flow is consistent with staging.
alternative_explanations: The file could have been downloaded from another source; the size match is strong but the file's origin is not directly recorded.
verifier_notes: an object of matching size reached this host, per records independent of it, shortly before a non-approved bulk transfer

findings.rationale: Tap flow from workstation 10.20.1.21 sent 23,180,407 bytes to 10.20.9.62:8080 in 15s, far above the 5MB bulk threshold and not an approved destination (approved: 10.20.0.45, 10.20.8.20). It follows a records-app export_bulk of patients_full by rhaddad from client 10.20.1.21 at 10:26:38 with bytes=23176722, which matches the size of the file later seen in Downloads.
assumptions: Bulk outbound to any destination not in the approved list violates policy, per the brief.
alternative_explanations: Flow records show 10.20.9.62:8080 also receives small routine traffic from several hosts, so the destination may be a known internal service; the policy issue rests on bulk size and the non-approved destination.
The flow is a simulated tap record; the payload is not confirmed as patient data by packet capture.
verifier_notes: bulk transfer to a destination not on the approved list, cited via the flow record

findings.rationale: The snapshot records mtime 10:28:56, about 53 seconds after the transfer ended, while the file's other timestamp is 2026-10-11 and the file size matches the 10:26 export. The snapshot is host-local and point-in-time, so the mtime could reflect a later legitimate write; this is weakly supported.
alternative_explanations: The file may have been written or touched by normal use after the upload.
The fs_stat snapshot is host-writable and taken at capture end, so it may not reflect the true sequence.
verifier_notes: an independent record shows the content arriving after the modification time the file carries
